concepts.name: Free legal aid and the Legal Services Authorities (NALSA)
concepts.description: Article 39A, the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, NALSA, the State, District, Taluk, High Court and Supreme Court legal services bodies, free legal services and eligible persons.
concepts.idea: Free legal aid reaches the poor through a statutory ladder of legal services bodies headed by NALSA.
concepts.rule: Article 39A provides for free legal aid to the poor and weaker sections, and Articles 14 and 22(1) oblige the State to ensure equality before law and equal opportunity. The Legal Services Authorities Act, enacted in 1987, came into force on 9 November 1995. NALSA monitors and evaluates legal aid programmes and lays down policies, principles and schemes; State Legal Services Authorities, High Court Legal Services Committees, District Authorities, Taluk Committees and the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee carry them out. Their main functions are free legal services, Lok Adalats and rural legal awareness camps. Free services include court fees, lawyers, certified copies and preparation of appeals. Eligible persons include women and children, SC/ST members, industrial workmen, disaster victims, the disabled, persons in custody and, by income according to the chapter, those earning up to Rs 1 lakh (Rs 5 lakh in the Supreme Court Committee) (pp.536-537).
concepts.example: A woman whose income is above the ceiling is still listed as eligible because women and children are a category in their own right.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional basis of legal aid in India:

1. Article 39A provides free legal aid only to persons in custody.
2. Articles 14 and 22(1) make it obligatory for the State to ensure equality before law and a legal system that promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity.
3. The Legal Services Authorities Act was enacted by Parliament to establish a nationwide uniform network for free and competent legal services to the weaker sections.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 39A provides for free legal aid to the poor and weaker sections of society, not only to persons in custody. Statement 2 is correct: Articles 14 and 22(1) make it obligatory for the State to ensure equality before law and a legal system that promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity. Statement 3 is correct: Parliament enacted the Legal Services Authorities Act to establish a nationwide uniform network for free and competent legal services to the weaker sections.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional and statutory basis of legal aid in India:

1. Articles 14 and 22(1) make it obligatory for the State to ensure equality before law and a legal system that promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity.
2. NALSA is a constitutional authority created directly by Article 39A.
3. The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 was enacted by the State Legislatures.

Statement 3 is incorrect: the Act was enacted by Parliament, not by the State Legislatures. So exactly 1 is correct.

'Only two statements' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statement 1).
'All three statements' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statement 1).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Legal Services Authorities Act:

1. It was enacted by Parliament in 1987.
2. It came into force on 9 November 1987.
3. It aims to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections on the basis of equal opportunity.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Parliament enacted the Legal Services Authorities Act in 1987. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act came into force on 9 November 1995, not 9 November 1987. Statement 3 is correct: the Act aims to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections on the basis of equal opportunity. So exactly 2 are correct.

concepts.name: Lok Adalats: meaning, organisation, jurisdiction and award
concepts.description: What a Lok Adalat is, its history, who organises it, its members, jurisdiction, referral, powers and the finality of its award.
concepts.idea: A Lok Adalat is a statutory people's forum that settles pending and pre-litigation compoundable disputes by compromise, and its award is a final decree.
concepts.rule: Lok Adalat means People's Court, based on Gandhian principles and part of ADR; the first post-independence camp was in Gujarat in 1982 and the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 gave it statutory status. The State, District, Supreme Court, High Court and Taluk legal services bodies may organise it; it generally has a judicial officer as chairman with a lawyer and a social worker. It settles cases pending before any court or matters not yet brought to court, but not offences that are not compoundable. A case may be referred if the parties agree, one party applies or the court is satisfied; pre-litigation disputes are referred by the organising agency on one party's application. It has civil court powers for summoning, discovery, affidavits and requisitioning records, and frames its own procedure. Its proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings (the chapter cites the IPC 1860, now the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023). Its award is deemed a civil court decree, final and binding, with no appeal (pp.537-539).
concepts.example: A cheque-bounce case pending in a court is referred to a Lok Adalat on one party's application and settled; the award is a decree and cannot be appealed.

o: A case relating to an offence that is not compoundable under any law
A case pending before any court
A matter within the jurisdiction of a court that has not been brought before it
A dispute referred on the application of one party to a pre-litigation matter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the organisation of Lok Adalats:

1. Only the National Legal Services Authority may organise Lok Adalats.
2. The organising agency may decide the intervals, places, jurisdiction and areas of the Lok Adalats it organises.
3. The Supreme Court Legal Services Committee may organise Lok Adalats.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the State, District, Supreme Court, High Court and Taluk legal services bodies may organise Lok Adalats along with NALSA. Statement 2 is correct: the organising agency holds Lok Adalats at such intervals and places and for such jurisdiction and areas as it thinks fit. Statement 3 is correct: the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee is among the organising agencies.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the members of a Lok Adalat:

1. The number of members is such as the agency organising the Lok Adalat may specify.
2. A Lok Adalat may consist only of serving judicial officers and of no other person.
3. Generally a judicial officer is chairman, with a lawyer and a social worker as members.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the number of members is whatever the organising agency specifies. Statement 2 is incorrect: a Lok Adalat consists of serving or retired judicial officers and other persons of the area, not of serving judicial officers alone. Statement 3 is correct: generally a judicial officer is chairman, with a lawyer and a social worker as members.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect.
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the jurisdiction of a Lok Adalat:

1. It can determine and arrive at a compromise or settlement in respect of any case pending before any court.
2. It can take up a matter falling within the jurisdiction of a court that has not yet been brought before that court.
3. It can decide a dispute and impose its decision even when one party does not agree to a settlement.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: a Lok Adalat can determine a compromise or settlement in respect of any case pending before any court. Statement 2 is correct: it can take up a matter falling within the jurisdiction of a court that has not yet been brought before that court. Statement 3 is incorrect: its jurisdiction is to determine a compromise or settlement between the parties; it cannot impose a decision where a party does not agree.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the reference of disputes to a Lok Adalat:

1. A pending case may be referred only when both parties jointly apply to the court.
2. A pre-litigation dispute can be referred only by a court.
3. A pre-litigation dispute can be referred by the agency organising the Lok Adalat on receipt of an application from any one of the parties.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: a pending case may also be referred when one party applies, or when the court is satisfied that the matter is appropriate, not only on a joint application. Statement 2 is incorrect: a pre-litigation dispute is referred by the agency organising the Lok Adalat on an application from any one of the parties, not only by a court. Statement 3 is correct: a pre-litigation dispute can be referred by the organising agency on receipt of an application from any one of the parties.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of a Lok Adalat while trying a suit:

1. It has the powers of a Civil Court to summon and enforce the attendance of any witness and examine him on oath.
2. It has the powers of a Civil Court in respect of the discovery and production of any document.
3. It has the powers of a Civil Court in respect of the reception of evidence on affidavits.
4. It has no power to requisition any public record or document from a court or office.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: it has the powers of a Civil Court to summon and enforce the attendance of any witness and examine him on oath. Statement 2 is correct: it has the powers of a Civil Court in respect of the discovery and production of any document. Statement 3 is correct: it has the powers of a Civil Court in respect of the reception of evidence on affidavits. Statement 4 is incorrect: it does have the power to requisition any public record or document from any court or office.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the procedure and status of Lok Adalat proceedings:

1. While trying a suit, a Lok Adalat has the powers of a High Court under the Constitution, such as issuing writs.
2. A Lok Adalat has the power to specify its own procedure for determining a dispute.
3. All proceedings before a Lok Adalat are deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code (1860) (now the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it has only the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure (1908) for specified matters, not the constitutional powers of a High Court such as issuing writs. Statement 2 is correct: a Lok Adalat has the power to specify its own procedure for determining a dispute. Statement 3 is correct: all proceedings before a Lok Adalat are deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code (1860) (now the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.

questions.q:

concepts.name: Types and benefits of Lok Adalats; Permanent Lok Adalats
concepts.description: National, State and Permanent Lok Adalats, the advantages of Lok Adalats and ADR, and the Permanent Lok Adalats for public utility services.
concepts.idea: Lok Adalats come in national, state and permanent forms, and the Permanent Lok Adalat decides public utility disputes up to a pecuniary limit.
concepts.rule: There are three types of Lok Adalats: National (held on one day in all courts from the Supreme Court to the Taluk level, monthly on a subject since 2015, according to the chapter), State or Regular (Continuous, Daily, Mobile and Mega) and Permanent. Their benefits include no court fee (refunded if paid), procedural flexibility, direct interaction with the judge, and a binding, non-appealable award. The Legal Services Authorities Act was amended in 2002 to create Permanent Lok Adalats for public utility services such as transport, postal and telephone services, power, water, sanitation, hospitals and insurance. Its chairman is or has been a district judge or higher, with two persons experienced in public utility services. Its pecuniary limit was Rs ten lakh and became Rs one crore in 2015; it has no jurisdiction over non-compoundable offences, bars courts after an application, and its award is final and by majority (pp.539-541).
concepts.example: A passenger's dispute with an airline for Rs 40 lakh can go to a Permanent Lok Adalat, and once she applies she cannot also sue in court.

concepts.name: Family Courts
concepts.description: The Family Courts Act 1984, why Family Courts were created, their objectives, features, jurisdiction and appeals.
concepts.idea: Family Courts are specialised, conciliation-first courts for marriage and family disputes with one appeal to the High Court.
concepts.rule: The Family Courts Act, 1984 provides for Family Courts to promote conciliation and speedy settlement of disputes relating to marriage and family affairs. They were demanded by women's associations and backed by the Law Commission's 59th Report (1974); the Code of Civil Procedure was amended in 1976 but courts made little use of it. State Governments establish them in consultation with the High Courts and must do so in every city or town with a population exceeding one million. They exclusively hear matrimonial relief, property of the spouses, legitimacy, guardianship and custody, and maintenance of wife, children and parents. The Court must first try reconciliation, with informal proceedings and counsellors, the parties have no right to a lawyer, evidence rules are simplified, and only one appeal lies, to the High Court (pp.541-543).
concepts.example: A wife's claim for maintenance and a husband's petition for divorce are heard by the Family Court, which first tries to reconcile them.

concepts.name: Gram Nyayalayas
concepts.description: The Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008: purpose, features, jurisdiction, procedure, appeals and the problems in establishing them.
concepts.idea: Gram Nyayalayas are mobile magistrate courts that take justice to villages with summary, conciliatory procedure.
concepts.rule: The Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008 provides access to justice at the doorstep, drawing on Article 39A and the Law Commission's 114th Report. A Gram Nyayalaya is a court of Judicial Magistrate of the first class, presided over by a Nyayadhikari appointed by the State Government in consultation with the High Court, with the same salary and powers as First Class Magistrates. It is set up for every intermediate-level Panchayat or group of contiguous Panchayats, is a mobile court with civil and criminal powers over matters in the First and Second Schedules, follows summary procedure in criminal trial, uses conciliators and is not bound, according to the chapter, by the Indian Evidence Act (since replaced by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023). Criminal appeals go to the Court of Session and civil appeals to the District Court, each within six months; plea bargaining is allowed. States establish them in consultation with High Courts; the Act does not make it mandatory, and the 2013 Conference left the decision to them (pp.543-545).
concepts.example: A Nyayadhikari travels from the intermediate Panchayat headquarters to a village to try a petty civil dispute and first tries conciliation.

concepts.name: Commercial Courts
concepts.description: The Commercial Courts Act 2015: forums, commercial dispute, specified value, reasons and pre-institution mediation.
concepts.idea: The Commercial Courts Act 2015 creates a hierarchy of courts and divisions for speedy resolution of commercial disputes of specified value.
concepts.rule: The Commercial Courts Act, 2015 provides for Commercial Courts, Commercial Appellate Courts, and a Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division in High Courts to decide commercial disputes of specified value, defined as disputes from ordinary transactions of merchants, bankers, financiers and traders. It rests on the Law Commission's 253rd Report and aims at early resolution of high value disputes and investor confidence. The State Government constitutes Commercial Courts at district level and designates Commercial Appellate Courts at district judge level, while the Chief Justice constitutes the Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division in High Courts with ordinary original civil jurisdiction. The specified value is not less than Rs 3 lakh, reduced in 2018 from Rs 1 crore. Mediation is compulsory before a suit that does not contemplate urgent interim relief, and Legal Services Authorities may be empowered for it (pp.545-546).
concepts.example: A partnership dispute above the specified value goes first to pre-institution mediation, and then to a Commercial Court.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Commercial Courts Act, 2015:

2. The Commercial Division of a High Court is constituted by the State Government.
3. It is meant for adjudicating commercial disputes of specified value.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 provides for Commercial Courts, Commercial Appellate Courts, Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division in the High Courts. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Chief Justice of the High Court, not the State Government, constitutes the Commercial Division. Statement 3 is correct: it is meant for adjudicating commercial disputes of specified value.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the specified value of commercial disputes:

1. The specified value shall not be less than Rs 3 lakh or such higher value as may be notified by the Central Government.
2. A higher specified value is notified by the High Court concerned.
3. The Central Government may notify a specified value lower than Rs 3 lakh.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the specified value shall not be less than Rs 3 lakh or such higher value as may be notified by the Central Government. Statement 2 is incorrect: a higher value is notified by the Central Government, not by the High Court. Statement 3 is incorrect: the value shall not be less than Rs 3 lakh; the Central Government may notify only a higher value.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Commercial Courts at the district level:

1. The State Government may constitute Commercial Courts at District level for commercial disputes of specified value.
2. With respect to High Courts having ordinary original civil jurisdiction, the State Government may constitute Commercial Courts at the District Judge level.
3. Commercial Courts below the High Court level can be constituted only by the High Courts, not by the State Government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the State Government may constitute Commercial Courts at District level for commercial disputes of specified value. Statement 2 is correct: with respect to High Courts having ordinary original civil jurisdiction, the State Government may constitute Commercial Courts at the District Judge level. Statement 3 is incorrect: the State Government, not the High Court, constitutes Commercial Courts below the High Court level.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Commercial Appellate Division of a High Court:

1. It is constituted by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.
2. It hears appeals against the orders of the Commercial Courts at the District judge level and the orders of the Commercial Division of that High Court.
3. It is constituted by the State Government on the advice of the Chief Justice.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Commercial Appellate Division is constituted by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. Statement 2 is correct: it hears appeals against the orders of the Commercial Courts at the District judge level and the orders of the Commercial Division of that High Court. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Chief Justice constitutes it, not the State Government.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect.

2. They are designated by the State Government at the District judge level.
3. They exercise appellate jurisdiction over the Commercial Courts below the district judge level.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Commercial Appellate Courts are designated except in the territories over which High Courts have ordinary original civil jurisdiction. Statement 2 is correct: they are designated by the State Government at the District judge level. Statement 3 is correct: they exercise appellate jurisdiction over the Commercial Courts below the district judge level.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about what counts as a commercial dispute:

1. It is limited to disputes between merchants, and excludes those involving bankers and financiers.
2. It includes disputes relating to mercantile documents, joint venture and partnership agreements, intellectual property rights and insurance.
3. It includes criminal offences committed in the course of trade.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: a commercial dispute covers the ordinary transactions of merchants, bankers, financiers and traders, not merchants alone. Statement 2 is correct: a commercial dispute includes disputes relating to mercantile documents, joint venture and partnership agreements, intellectual property rights and insurance. Statement 3 is incorrect: commercial disputes are civil-type disputes arising out of transactions, not criminal offences.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.

3. Early resolution of commercial disputes would create a positive image to the investor world about the Indian legal system.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: high value commercial disputes involve complex facts and questions of law, so an independent mechanism was needed for their early resolution. Statement 2 is correct: all suits, appeals or applications related to commercial disputes of specified value are to be dealt with by the Commercial Courts or the Commercial Division of the High Courts. Statement 3 is correct: early resolution of commercial disputes would create a positive image to the investor world about the Indian legal system.

2. It was expected to accelerate economic growth and improve the international image of the Indian justice delivery system.
3. It was expected to improve the faith of the investor world in the legal culture of the nation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Bill was based on the 253rd Report of the Law Commission, not the 114th. Statement 2 is correct: it was expected to accelerate economic growth and improve the international image of the Indian justice delivery system. Consider the following statements about pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015:

2. Mediation is compulsory even for suits that seek urgent interim relief.
3. The Central Government may empower the Authorities constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 for pre-institution mediation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: mediation is compulsory before the institution of a suit that does not contemplate any urgent interim relief. Statement 2 is incorrect: the mediation requirement applies to a suit which does not contemplate urgent interim relief, not to suits seeking it. Statement 3 is correct: the Central Government may empower the Authorities constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 for pre-institution mediation.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

1. In 2018 it was reduced from the earlier Rs 1 crore to Rs 3 lakh.
2. The Central Government may notify a higher value.
3. The 2015 Act itself fixed it at Rs 3 lakh.
4. Each State Government fixes the value for its own Commercial Courts.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: in 2018 the specified value was reduced from the earlier Rs 1 crore to Rs 3 lakh. Statement 2 is correct: the Central Government may notify a higher value. Statement 3 is incorrect: Rs 3 lakh came by the reduction of 2018; the 2015 Act had originally fixed Rs 1 crore. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Central Government, not each State Government, may notify a higher value. So exactly 2 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following forums under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015:

1. Commercial Courts.
2. Commercial Appellate Courts.
3. Commercial Division of High Courts.
4. A Commercial Division in every High Court, whether or not it has ordinary original civil jurisdiction.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Commercial Courts are a forum under the Act. Statement 2 is correct: Commercial Appellate Courts are a forum under the Act. Statement 3 is correct: the Commercial Division of High Courts is a forum under the Act. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Chief Justice may constitute a Commercial Division only in High Courts having ordinary original civil jurisdiction, not in every High Court. So exactly 3 are correct.

'Only two statements' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2 and 3).
'All four statements' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2 and 3).

Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A separate Commercial Courts mechanism was proposed for high value commercial disputes.
Statement-II: High value commercial disputes involve complex facts and questions of law and therefore need an independent mechanism for early resolution.

o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct. Because high value commercial disputes involve complex facts and questions of law, there is a need for an independent mechanism for their early resolution, and so a separate Commercial Courts mechanism was proposed; II explains I.
